headline: No 'deposit haircut': Depositors to get money back with interest, says Finance Minister
summary: Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury assures parliament that bank depositors will receive full deposits plus interest, removing the 'haircut' provision.
details: Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury assured parliament today that depositors of banks burdened with defaulted loans will receive their full deposits along with interest.
Responding to a notice from BNP MP Rehena Akhter Ranu, the minister stated that the 'haircut' provision—which reduces the value of deposits during a banking crisis—will be removed.
To stabilize the financial sector, five banks have been merged under the Bank Resolution Act to form the Consolidated Islami Bank.
Under the Depositor Protection Act 2026, the maximum protected deposit limit has been increased from Tk 100,000 to Tk 200,000.
A special forensic audit is currently underway to identify those responsible for irregular investments in the five merged banks to recover assets.
The government is pursuing asset recovery through civil cases and international legal firms on a 'no win, no fee' basis to recover laundered loans.
Civil proceedings have already begun against six priority groups, including S Alam, Beximco, and Saifuzzaman Chowdhury.
The minister acknowledged the hardship of depositors, describing the situation as 'heartbreaking' and urged patience as the recovery process takes time.
caption:
No 'deposit haircut' for bank depositors! The Finance Minister has assured that all deposits and interest will be returned.

Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury assured parliament today that depositors of banks burdened with defaulted loans will receive their full deposits along with interest.

Responding to a notice from BNP MP Rehena Akhter Ranu, the minister stated that the 'haircut' provision—which reduces the value of deposits during a banking crisis—will be removed.

To stabilize the financial sector, five banks have been merged under the Bank Resolution Act to form the Consolidated Islami Bank.

Under the Depositor Protection Act 2026, the maximum protected deposit limit has been increased from Tk 100,000 to Tk 200,000.

A special forensic audit is currently underway to identify those responsible for irregular investments in the five merged banks to recover assets.

The government is pursuing asset recovery through civil cases and international legal firms on a 'no win, no fee' basis to recover laundered loans.

Civil proceedings have already begun against six priority groups, including S Alam, Beximco, and Saifuzzaman Chowdhury.

The minister acknowledged the hardship of depositors, describing the situation as 'heartbreaking' and urged patience as the recovery process takes time.

headline: Opposition leader named chair of Public Accounts Committee in Parliament
summary: Syed Abdullah Mohammed Taher becomes the first Jamaat lawmaker to lead a parliamentary standing committee, overseeing public expenditure and accountability.
details: Parliament has constituted a 15-member Standing Committee on Public Accounts, appointing Opposition Deputy Leader Syed Abdullah Mohammed Taher as its chairman.
This appointment is historic, marking the first time a lawmaker from Jamaat-e-Islami has been named the chairman of a parliamentary standing committee.
The proposal to form the committee was placed by Chief Whip Mohammad Nurul Islam and was unanimously adopted under the chairmanship of Deputy Speaker Kayser Kamal.
The Public Accounts Committee is one of the most critical standing committees in Parliament, responsible for overseeing public expenditure and ensuring accountability in public accounts.
The committee's role involves reviewing government spending after the passage of the national budget, scrutinizing irregularities in audit reports, and examining how agencies respond to findings.
The decision follows discussions of the National Consensus Commission, where it was agreed that the Public Accounts Committee would be one of four committees chaired by the opposition.
caption:
A historic first for Jamaat-e-Islami: an opposition leader now leads one of Parliament's most powerful oversight committees.

Parliament has constituted a 15-member Standing Committee on Public Accounts, appointing Opposition Deputy Leader Syed Abdullah Mohammed Taher as its chairman.

This appointment is historic, marking the first time a lawmaker from Jamaat-e-Islami has been named the chairman of a parliamentary standing committee.

The proposal to form the committee was placed by Chief Whip Mohammad Nurul Islam and was unanimously adopted under the chairmanship of Deputy Speaker Kayser Kamal.

The Public Accounts Committee is one of the most critical standing committees in Parliament, responsible for overseeing public expenditure and ensuring accountability in public accounts.

The committee's role involves reviewing government spending after the passage of the national budget, scrutinizing irregularities in audit reports, and examining how agencies respond to findings.

The decision follows discussions of the National Consensus Commission, where it was agreed that the Public Accounts Committee would be one of four committees chaired by the opposition.
